# Releasing Hey Reachy

Signed artifacts are produced locally; CI only publishes the GitHub release with
generated notes. Credentials never enter the repository or CI.

## One-time setup

1. **App Store Connect API key** — App Store Connect → Users and Access →
   Integrations → App Store Connect API → Team Keys, role **App Manager**.
   Download the `.p8` once and write the credentials file:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/.config/reachy-mini
   cat > ~/.config/reachy-mini/release.env <<'CONF'
   REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=XXXXXXXXXX
   REACHY_ASC_KEY_ID=XXXXXXXXXX
   REACHY_ASC_ISSUER_ID=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
   REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH=/Users/you/.config/reachy-mini/AuthKey_XXXXXXXXXX.p8
   CONF
   ```

2. **App IDs and the App Group** — the first signed build with
   `-allowProvisioningUpdates` registers the bundle ids
   (`com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`, `.Widget`), but the
   `group.com.alexey1312.ReachyMini` capability must be added by hand in
   Xcode's Signing & Capabilities, once per App ID (app and widget separately,
   iOS and macOS separately). `xcodebuild` cannot create it.

3. **App Store Connect app record** — My Apps → New App:
   - Name: **Hey Reachy**; if taken, fall back to “Hey Reachy — robot remote”.
   - Subtitle: **Control your Reachy Mini**.
   - Bundle id `com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`.
   - The description must state it is an unofficial client for Reachy Mini by
     Pollen Robotics. A public TestFlight link goes through Beta App Review, so
     the name is checked before any App Store submission.
   - App Privacy: no data collected. The app talks to the robot on the local
     network and to Hugging Face with the user's own OAuth session; nothing is
     sent to the developer.
   - Encryption: answered in the Info.plist (`ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption`),
     ASC asks nothing per build.

4. **Developer ID Application certificate** (macOS) — Xcode → Settings →
   Accounts → Manage Certificates → “+” → Developer ID Application.

5. **macOS ships through both channels**, so the Mac App Store one needs its own
   signing assets besides the Developer ID certificate: Apple Distribution and
   Mac Installer Distribution. `-allowProvisioningUpdates` creates them through
   the Xcode account the same way it does for iOS. The app record already
   carries a macOS platform beside the iOS one — `mise run asc -- versions list
   --app 6799644194` shows both — so nothing has to be created in App Store
   Connect. What is not automatic is the App Group: step 2 registers it per App
   ID, and the macOS App ID is a separate one from the iOS App ID.

## Each release

1. Bump `MARKETING_VERSION` in `Apps/Project.swift` (bare semver, e.g. `0.2.0`)
   and land it on `main`. Build numbers are the commit count — nothing to bump.
2. Tag and push; the tag triggers the GitHub release with git-cliff notes:

   ```bash
   git tag 0.2.0 && git push origin 0.2.0
   ```

3. Produce and ship the artifacts:


content.text:
Создал группу и просмотрел состояние ASC. Идея хорошая, но между «создать группу» и «кнопка в README» стоит Beta App Review — расскажу, что уже сделано и что упирается в тебя.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Публичная ссылка — это не отдельная сущность, а два атрибута **внешней** beta-группы: `publicLinkEnabled` и `publicLinkLimit`. Внутренняя группа (`isInternalGroup: true`, как ваша `Internal`) их не поддерживает в принципе — поэтому нужна была новая группа.
- Внешнее тестирование — единственная часть TestFlight, которая проходит ревью Apple. Внутренние тестеры получают билд сразу после обработки; внешние — только после того, как конкретный билд получил `betaAppReviewSubmission` со статусом approved.
- Ревью привязано к **билду**, а не к приложению: iOS 110 и macOS 110 — два отдельных сабмита. Но первое одобрение самое дорогое; последующие билды той же версии обычно проходят автоматически.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Что сделано

Внешняя группа **Public Beta** создана: `c48f6abb-c178-40a2-8747-b6513add766e` (feedback включён). Это обратимо — `asc testflight groups delete`.

## Что мешает включить ссылку прямо сейчас

Проверил три места, и все три пустые:

| Что | Состояние | Кто может заполнить |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `betaAppLocalizations` | `[]` — нет описания, feedback email, privacy policy URL | нужен твой текст + URL |
| `betaAppReviewDetails` | `attributes: {}` — нет контакта для ревьюера | только ты (имя, email, телефон) |
| `betaAppReviewSubmission` для билда 110 | не существует | я, после первых двух |

Оба билда 110 (iOS и macOS, версия 0.1.1) в состоянии `VALID` — они готовы, их просто некуда отправить.

Включить `--public-link-enabled` можно и сегодня, но ссылка будет вести на страницу, где человек присоединяется и не может ничего скачать. Поэтому порядок: метаданные → ревью → ссылка → README.

## Два риска, которые стоит назвать заранее

**Ревьюеру нечего тестировать.** У Apple нет Reachy Mini. Без робота приложение показывает connect gate и всё. Это самая частая причина отказа на Beta App Review для железо-зависимых клиентов — и это ровно то место, где нужен твой текст, а не мой.

**Имя.** `docs/release.md:35` уже фиксирует, что публичная ссылка — первый момент, когда Apple смотрит на название. «Hey Reachy» + описание, ссылающееся на Reachy Mini и Pollen Robotics, — это использование чужого товарного знака. Дисклеймер о неаффилированности в описании обязателен (он уже есть в README, надо продублировать в Test Information).

## Что мне нужно от тебя

**1. Контакт для ревью** — имя, фамилия, email, телефон в международном формате. Их я выдумать не могу, они уйдут в `asc testflight review edit`.

**2. Review Notes — тут твоё знание железа решает исход.** Ревьюеру надо за пару минут объяснить, что приложение управляет физическим роботом, которого у него нет, и что именно он *может* проверить без робота. Варианты, между которыми стоит выбрать:

- честно «hardware required», плюс ссылка на демо-видео (в README оно ещё «on its way» — то есть его надо снять);
- дать ему точку входа без железа: `sim-daemon` он не запустит, но, возможно, есть состояние, которое воспроизводится само;
- поднять симулятор на публично доступном хосте на время ревью — быстро, но это выставляет наружу порт 8000, а `README.md:128` прямо это запрещает.

Я склоняюсь к первому + видео. Но чего именно ревьюер добьётся, запустив приложение без робота, знаешь ты.

**3. Privacy policy URL.** В репозитории его нет, а для внешнего тестирования он обязателен. Предлагаю `docs/privacy.md` со ссылкой на GitHub — содержание уже сформулировано в `docs/release.md:36-38` («no data collected»). Могу написать.

**4. Лимит на ссылку.** Потолок внешних тестеров — 10 000 на приложение, и он общий. Публичная ссылка без лимита исчерпывает его молча. Предложил бы `--public-link-limit 500` на старте — поднять одной командой, опустить после того, как люди пришли, уже нельзя осмысленно.

Дай ответы на 1–3, и я прогоняю метаданные, отправляю оба билда в ревью и готовлю README-секцию с бейджем — она встанет между «Getting started» и «Development without hardware», а сам URL подставится, когда ревью пройдёт.

input.prompt:
In this repo (/Users/aleksei/Developer/reachy-mini-desktop-app-swift), a SwiftUI app "Hey Reachy" is a network client for a physical Reachy Mini robot.

I need to know precisely what a person who launches the app WITHOUT any robot on the network can actually see and interact with. This is for App Store Connect Beta App Review notes, so accuracy matters.

Search medium-thoroughly in Sources/ReachyUI (especially the connect gate / root view) and Apps/. Answer:
1. What screen appears on first launch with no robot present? What does it show while discovery finds nothing (empty state text, buttons)?
2. Can the user enter a manual host/address? Is there any onboarding, Bluetooth setup flow, or Hugging Face sign-in reachable without a robot?
3. Is there any demo/mock/offline mode, sample data, or a way to explore the tabs without a connection?
4. Which permission prompts appear on launch (local network, bluetooth, camera, microphone) and when.
5. Anything a reviewer could plausibly evaluate without hardware.

Be concrete and cite file:line. Do not speculate — if something is not there, say so.

content.text:
## 1. First launch with no robot: what's on screen

The root view forks on `session.phase`; with nothing connected it renders `ConnectGate`, never the tab shell — `Sources/ReachyUI/ReachyRootView.swift:98-166` (`isConnectedEnough`, `.idle`/`.connecting` → gate).

`ConnectGate` (`Sources/ReachyUI/Connect/ConnectGate.swift:14-43`) is a `NavigationStack` titled **"Connect"** (:39) with a Hugging Face account button in the leading toolbar slot (:40).

Inside, `ConnectionScreen` (`Sources/ReachyUI/ConnectionScreen.swift:93-142`) shows, top to bottom:

- **Header** (`Connect/ConnectHeader.swift:39-50`): status line — with nothing connected it reads **"Not connected"** (:146); during an automatic attempt **"Connecting to robot"/"Connecting to <host>"** (:148); after a failed attempt **"Couldn't connect to <host>"** (:143).
- **Progress rail**, three nodes captioned **Daemon / Version / Backend** (`Connect/ConnectRail.swift:101-107`), permanently mounted plus one reserved caption line (:39-52).
- **Segmented picker**: **"This network" | "Hugging Face" | "Manual"** (`Connect/ConnectRoute.swift:23-29`, picker at :36-48).
- **"This network" (default segment)** — `Connect/NetworkRobotsSection.swift`: with nothing found it shows a grey **"Searching…"** row (:32-35) and a footer of two paragraphs: *"Your Reachy Mini appears below once it is powered on and joined to this Wi-Fi network."* (:69) and *"Known addresses are retried every 10 s. A robot whose daemon isn't running answers nothing on the network — power it on, or enter its address below."* (:71-77). If the user cancelled an attempt, an extra **"Automatic reconnect paused"** row appears (:28-31). No robot rows on a fresh install (`entries` comes from previously-handshaken robots).
- **A permanent "Set up a new robot over Bluetooth" button** in its own section, never disabled (`ConnectionScreen.swift:196-213`, button at :209).
- **Privacy section**: a **"Privacy permissions"** button always (`ConnectionScreen.swift:162`), plus — only if the Bonjour browser reported policy denial — **"Local Network permission denied"**, an **"Open Settings"** deep link and *"Without it this app cannot find the robot or reach it at a typed address."* (:154-168).
- **Error row**: the last connection error, suppressed while the automatic 10 s sweep is running (`ConnectionScreen.swift:183-192`).

Failure buttons appear only in terminal states: **"Try again" + "Cancel"** after a failed LAN attempt, **"Start robot backend" / "Continue anyway" / "Cancel"** if a daemon answered but its backend is down (`ConnectHeader.swift:69-89`). None of these can be reached without hardware/a daemon.

**Important for review notes:** on a truly first launch (no stored address, onboarding never seen) the app *auto-presents the Bluetooth onboarding sheet over the connect screen* — `ConnectionScreen.swift:226-228`. Cancelling it sets the flag so it does not reappear (`Onboarding/OnboardingModel.swift:235-238`). The XCUITest cold-launch expectation of the gate (`Apps/ReachyMiniUITests/Sources/SmokeTests.swift:18-32`) runs with `--reachy-smoke`, which skips `appeared()` entirely, so it does not exercise that sheet.

## 2. Manual host, onboarding, Bluetooth, Hugging Face — all reachable with no robot

- **Manual address: yes.** "Manual" segment → text field placeholder **"host, host:port, or IP"**, a **Connect** button disabled until the string parses, and a warning footer *"The daemon uses unencrypted HTTP without authentication. Connect only on a trusted private network."* (`Connect/ManualAddressSection.swift:16-39`). The field is pre-filled with the last successful address if there is one (`ConnectionScreen.swift:56`).
- **Bluetooth onboarding: yes, fully browsable.** "Set up a new robot over Bluetooth" opens `OnboardingFlow` (`Onboarding/OnboardingFlow.swift:9-59`): Welcome → Scan → PIN → Network → Joining → Handoff. The Welcome screen is static text listing prerequisites and warns *"The next screen turns on Bluetooth scanning, so iOS will ask for permission."* (`Onboarding/OnboardingWelcomeStep.swift:41-46`). Tapping **Start** (:49) is the first CoreBluetooth call. On the Simulator the scan step renders a `ContentUnavailableView` *"This device has no Bluetooth" / "The iOS Simulator never has any…"* (`Onboarding/OnboardingScanStep.swift:36-47`); on a device it shows a spinner and **"Searching…"** with no results (:88-93). Steps past Scan require a real robot advertising.
- **Hugging Face sign-in: yes, and it works with no robot.** Toolbar account button on the gate (`Settings/HFAccountToolbarButton.swift:70-83`) opens `HFSignInScreen` (`Navigation/RootSheets.swift:28-37`), which offers **"Sign in with Hugging Face"** (ASWebAuthenticationSession OAuth; the client ID is configured, `Sources/HuggingFaceAuth/HFOAuth.swift:42`, gate at :59 and `Settings/HFSignInModel.swift:42-44`) and a **"Use an access token"** disclosure with a `hf_…` secure field (`Settings/HFAccountSection.swift:96-121`). The robot-linking half is hidden without a connection (`HFAccountSection.swift:56`).
- **"Your Reachies" (remote robots): yes.** Hugging Face segment → **"Your Reachies / Through Hugging Face"** row (`Remote/YourReachiesSection.swift:16-32`) → sheet listing robots on the HF relay. Signed out it shows *"Not signed in — Sign in to Hugging Face to reach robots linked to your account."*; signed in with none online, *"No Reachy online"* + Refresh (`Remote/YourReachiesScreen.swift:84-120`). This segment is deliberately never disabled by the discovery sweep (`ConnectionScreen.swift:124-135`).
- **Privacy screen: yes** — see §4.

## 3. Demo / mock / offline mode: none

There is no demo, mock, sample-data or offline mode in the shipping app. The only "frozen" path is `reachyPreviewMode` (`Sources/ReachyUI/PreviewMode.swift:24-29`), enabled solely by the launch argument `--reachy-smoke` (`Apps/ReachyMini/Sources/ReachyMiniApp.swift:24`) — a launch argument only XCUITest/Xcode can pass, not reachable from a TestFlight install, and it *suppresses* work rather than supplying fake data. Everything else preview-related (`Sources/ReachyUI/Previews/`, `ReachyStorybook` target) is excluded from the SwiftPM target and is a separate app target, not part of "Hey Reachy".

**The tabs cannot be explored without a connection.** The five-tab shell (`ReachyTabShell`) is only instantiated when `isConnectedEnough` is true (`ReachyRootView.swift:100-112`), i.e. a real `.connected(identity)` from a handshake — or `.unreachable`, which can only be reached *after* a successful connection. Settings, Live, Moves, Apps, Robot, the developer/device-check screen (`Apps/ReachyMini/Sources/DeviceCheckView.swift`, injected into Settings → Advanced at `ReachyRootView.swift:119`) and the BLE console (`Settings/AdvancedSettingsSection.swift:61`) are therefore all unreachable without hardware or a daemon.

Note: a locally-run simulated daemon counts as a robot — `CandidateSweep` probes `127.0.0.1` on macOS/Simulator only (`Connect/CandidateSweep.swift:88-92`); on a physical iPhone the static candidate is `reachy-mini.local` alone (:86).

## 4. Permission prompts

Declared usage strings (`Apps/Project.swift:71-99`, materialized in `Apps/Derived/InfoPlists/ReachyMini-Info.plist`): Bluetooth-Always, Local Network + `NSBonjourServices` (`_reachy-mini._tcp`, `_http._tcp`), Microphone, Camera, and `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`.

- **Local Network — on launch, immediately and unprompted by any user action.** `ConnectionScreen.appeared()` starts the Bonjour browsers and the candidate sweep as soon as the connect screen appears (`ConnectionScreen.swift:215-229`); `RobotBrowser.start()` runs two `NWBrowser`s (`Sources/ReachyKit/Transport/RobotBrowser.swift:59-88`) and the sweep dials `reachy-mini.local` over HTTP. Both trigger the system Local Network alert. On a first launch this alert lands under/behind the auto-presented onboarding sheet. This is the one prompt a reviewer will definitely see.
- **Bluetooth — only after two explicit taps**: "Set up a new robot over Bluetooth" → **Start** on the Welcome screen (`OnboardingWelcomeStep.swift:49` → `OnboardingModel.beginScan()`), or the **Allow** button on the Privacy screen (`Settings/Permissions/PermissionsScreen.swift:92-96,108`). Opening the Privacy screen itself never prompts — it reads `CBCentralManager.authorization`, which builds no central (`PermissionsScreen.swift:14-16,48-60`).
- **Microphone — only via an explicit tap**: the Privacy screen's **Allow** row (`PermissionsScreen.swift:110` → `MicrophonePermission.request()`, `Sources/ReachyMedia/MicrophonePermission.swift:44-46`) or the two-way-audio path in `Sources/ReachyMedia/CameraSession.swift:157`, which requires a connected robot's video stream.
- **Camera — never prompted.** There is no `AVCaptureDevice` video request or local capturer anywhere in `Sources/` (grep for `for: .video` / `RTCCameraVideoCapturer` returns nothing); the robot's camera arrives over WebRTC. The `NSCameraUsageDescription` string is declared defensively and says so: *"Hey Reachy never records with your phone's camera; the robot video stack references this API."* (`Apps/Project.swift:71-77`). (Note `Sources/ReachyUI/Settings/Permissions/PermissionKind.swift:10-12` claims the project declares no camera key — that comment is stale; the key *is* declared and ships.)
- The Privacy screen lists exactly three permissions — Bluetooth, Local network, Microphone (`PermissionKind.swift:13-16`) — with a "why" under each and a Settings deep link when refused.

## 5. What a reviewer can actually evaluate without hardware

Concretely reachable and functional with no robot on the network:

1. The **Connect gate** in full: header/rail, all three segments, the "Searching…" empty state and its explanatory copy, the manual-address field with live validation of the Connect button, and the unencrypted-HTTP warning.
2. A **manual connect attempt** to any typed host — it will fail and exercise the terminal-failure UI ("Couldn't connect to …", "Try again", "Cancel"), which is real, observable behaviour.
3. The **Privacy permissions screen** end to end, including granting/refusing Local Network, Bluetooth and Microphone and the "Open Settings" deep links.
4. The **Bluetooth setup flow's** first two screens (Welcome prerequisites; Scan showing "Searching…", or the explicit "This device has no Bluetooth" state on Simulator), plus Cancel.

## 1. First launch with no robot: what's on screen

The root view forks on `session.phase`; with nothing connected it renders `ConnectGate`, never the tab shell — `Sources/ReachyUI/ReachyRootView.swift:98-166` (`isConnectedEnough`, `.idle`/`.connecting` → gate).

`ConnectGate` (`Sources/ReachyUI/Connect/ConnectGate.swift:14-43`) is a `NavigationStack` titled **"Connect"** (:39) with a Hugging Face account button in the leading toolbar slot (:40).

Inside, `ConnectionScreen` (`Sources/ReachyUI/ConnectionScreen.swift:93-142`) shows, top to bottom:

- **Header** (`Connect/ConnectHeader.swift:39-50`): status line — with nothing connected it reads **"Not connected"** (:146); during an automatic attempt **"Connecting to robot"/"Connecting to <host>"** (:148); after a failed attempt **"Couldn't connect to <host>"** (:143).
- **Progress rail**, three nodes captioned **Daemon / Version / Backend** (`Connect/ConnectRail.swift:101-107`), permanently mounted plus one reserved caption line (:39-52).
- **Segmented picker**: **"This network" | "Hugging Face" | "Manual"** (`Connect/ConnectRoute.swift:23-29`, picker at :36-48).
- **"This network" (default segment)** — `Connect/NetworkRobotsSection.swift`: with nothing found it shows a grey **"Searching…"** row (:32-35) and a footer of two paragraphs: *"Your Reachy Mini appears below once it is powered on and joined to this Wi-Fi network."* (:69) and *"Known addresses are retried every 10 s. A robot whose daemon isn't running answers nothing on the network — power it on, or enter its address below."* (:71-77). If the user cancelled an attempt, an extra **"Automatic reconnect paused"** row appears (:28-31). No robot rows on a fresh install (`entries` comes from previously-handshaken robots).
- **A permanent "Set up a new robot over Bluetooth" button** in its own section, never disabled (`ConnectionScreen.swift:196-213`, button at :209).
- **Privacy section**: a **"Privacy permissions"** button always (`ConnectionScreen.swift:162`), plus — only if the Bonjour browser reported policy denial — **"Local Network permission denied"**, an **"Open Settings"** deep link and *"Without it this app cannot find the robot or reach it at a typed address."* (:154-168).
- **Error row**: the last connection error, suppressed while the automatic 10 s sweep is running (`ConnectionScreen.swift:183-192`).

Failure buttons appear only in terminal states: **"Try again" + "Cancel"** after a failed LAN attempt, **"Start robot backend" / "Continue anyway" / "Cancel"** if a daemon answered but its backend is down (`ConnectHeader.swift:69-89`). None of these can be reached without hardware/a daemon.

**Important for review notes:** on a truly first launch (no stored address, onboarding never seen) the app *auto-presents the Bluetooth onboarding sheet over the connect screen* — `ConnectionScreen.swift:226-228`. Cancelling it sets the flag so it does not reappear (`Onboarding/OnboardingModel.swift:235-238`). The XCUITest cold-launch expectation of the gate (`Apps/ReachyMiniUITests/Sources/SmokeTests.swift:18-32`) runs with `--reachy-smoke`, which skips `appeared()` entirely, so it does not exercise that sheet.

- **Manual address: yes.** "Manual" segment → text field placeholder **"host, host:port, or IP"**, a **Connect** button disabled until the string parses, and a warning footer *"The daemon uses unencrypted HTTP without authentication. - **Bluetooth onboarding: yes, fully browsable.** "Set up a new robot over Bluetooth" opens `OnboardingFlow` (`Onboarding/OnboardingFlow.swift:9-59`): Welcome → Scan → PIN → Network → Joining → Handoff. The Welcome screen is static text listing prerequisites and warns *"The next screen turns on Bluetooth scanning, so iOS will ask for permission."* (`Onboarding/OnboardingWelcomeStep.swift:41-46`). Tapping **Start** (:49) is the first CoreBluetooth call. On the Simulator the scan step renders a `ContentUnavailableView` *"This device has no Bluetooth" / "The iOS Simulator never has any…"* (`Onboarding/OnboardingScanStep.swift:36-47`); on a device it shows a spinner and **"Searching…"** with no results (:88-93). Steps past Scan require a real robot advertising.
- **Hugging Face sign-in: yes, and it works with no robot.** Toolbar account button on the gate (`Settings/HFAccountToolbarButton.swift:70-83`) opens `HFSignInScreen` (`Navigation/RootSheets.swift:28-37`), which offers **"Sign in with Hugging Face"** (ASWebAuthenticationSession OAuth; the client ID is configured, `Sources/HuggingFaceAuth/HFOAuth.swift:42`, gate at :59 and `Settings/HFSignInModel.swift:42-44`) and a **"Use an access token"** disclosure with a `hf_…` secure field (`Settings/HFAccountSection.swift:96-121`). The robot-linking half is hidden without a connection (`HFAccountSection.swift:56`).
- **"Your Reachies" (remote robots): yes.** Hugging Face segment → **"Your Reachies / Through Hugging Face"** row (`Remote/YourReachiesSection.swift:16-32`) → sheet listing robots on the HF relay. Signed out it shows *"Not signed in — Sign in to Hugging Face to reach robots linked to your account."*; signed in with none online, *"No Reachy online"* + Refresh (`Remote/YourReachiesScreen.swift:84-120`). This segment is deliberately never disabled by the discovery sweep (`ConnectionScreen.swift:124-135`).

There is no demo, mock, sample-data or offline mode in the shipping app. The only "frozen" path is `reachyPreviewMode` (`Sources/ReachyUI/PreviewMode.swift:24-29`), enabled solely by the launch argument `--reachy-smoke` (`Apps/ReachyMini/Sources/ReachyMiniApp.swift:24`) — a launch argument only XCUITest/Xcode can pass, not reachable from a TestFlight install, and it *suppresses* work rather than supplying fake data. 5. **Hugging Face sign-in** (browser OAuth or pasted token) and **"Your Reachies"** with its signed-out / empty / error states — the only network feature that works end to end without a robot, though it will list nothing unless the account owns an online robot.
6. Cosmetics that don't need a session: light/dark, Dynamic Type, VoiceOver labels on the gate, iPad/iPhone layout (the form is width-limited on iPad, `ConnectGate.swift:31`).

Hey Reachy is a network client for the Reachy Mini Wireless, a physical desktop robot made by Pollen Robotics. It is an unofficial, independent client, not affiliated with or endorsed by Pollen Robotics, and it talks only to the robot's own HTTP/WebSocket daemon over the local network.

1. Connect screen. Three segments: "This network" (Bonjour discovery, which will stay on "Searching..."), "Hugging Face", and "Manual". Under Manual, type any host and tap Connect to exercise the real failure path ("Couldn't connect to ...", Try again, Cancel).

# Privacy Policy — Hey Reachy

Last updated: 10 August 2026.

**Hey Reachy collects nothing.** There is no server behind this app, no account with the developer, no analytics, no
crash reporting SDK and no advertising. Nothing you do in the app is sent anywhere the app does not need to reach to
do its job.

## What the app talks to

**Your robot.** The app is a client for the daemon that runs on the Reachy Mini Wireless itself. Commands, the state
stream, camera and audio, the recorded moves, the file browser — all of it goes directly between your device and your
robot over your own network. None of it passes through the developer.

**Hugging Face, only if you sign in.** Signing in is optional and drives three features: installing robot apps from
Hugging Face Spaces, listing robots your account has linked, and reaching a robot outside its network through the
Hugging Face relay. The session is between your device and huggingface.co under your own account; the token is stored
in the system Keychain on your device and can be removed by signing out. See
[Hugging Face's privacy policy](https://huggingface.co/privacy) for what they do with it.

**Apple, for the platform features you use.** TestFlight feedback and crash reports go to Apple and are governed by
Apple's own terms. The app itself sends nothing to Apple beyond what any app does.

## What stays on your device

Robot addresses and identities, your preferences, the Hugging Face token (in the Keychain) and any files you download
from the robot. Deleting the app removes them.

## Permissions

| Permission        | Why                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Local Network** | To find your robot over Bonjour and reach its daemon. The app scans for robots, not for anything else. |
| **Bluetooth**     | Only to put a new robot onto Wi-Fi, and only from that setup flow.                                     |
| **Microphone**    | Only to speak through the robot's speaker during a live session.                                       |
| **Camera**        | Never used to record. The permission string is declared because the WebRTC stack that receives the robot's video references the API. |

## Children

The app is not directed at children and collects no data from anyone, of any age.

## Changes

Changes to this policy are committed to this file, in
[the public repository](https://github.com/alexey1312/reachy-mini-swift), with the full history visible.

## Contact

Aleksei Kakoulin — akakoulin.dev@gmail.com, or an issue on
[GitHub](https://github.com/alexey1312/reachy-mini-swift/issues).

because the app has no accounts.

```bash

  --locale en-US --whats-new "..."
```

# Releasing Hey Reachy

Signed artifacts are produced locally; CI only publishes the GitHub release with
generated notes. Credentials never enter the repository or CI.

## One-time setup

1. **App Store Connect API key** — App Store Connect → Users and Access →
   Integrations → App Store Connect API → Team Keys, role **App Manager**.
   Download the `.p8` once and write the credentials file:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/.config/reachy-mini
   cat > ~/.config/reachy-mini/release.env <<'CONF'
   REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=XXXXXXXXXX
   REACHY_ASC_KEY_ID=XXXXXXXXXX
   REACHY_ASC_ISSUER_ID=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
   REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH=/Users/you/.config/reachy-mini/AuthKey_XXXXXXXXXX.p8
   CONF
   ```

2. **App IDs and the App Group** — the first signed build with
   `-allowProvisioningUpdates` registers the bundle ids
   (`com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`, `.Widget`), but the
   `group.com.alexey1312.ReachyMini` capability must be added by hand in
   Xcode's Signing & Capabilities, once per App ID (app and widget separately,
   iOS and macOS separately). `xcodebuild` cannot create it.

3. **App Store Connect app record** — My Apps → New App:
   - Name: **Hey Reachy**; if taken, fall back to “Hey Reachy — robot remote”.
   - Subtitle: **Control your Reachy Mini**.
   - Bundle id `com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`.
   - The description must state it is an unofficial client for Reachy Mini by
     Pollen Robotics. A public TestFlight link goes through Beta App Review, so
     the name is checked before any App Store submission.
   - App Privacy: no data collected. The app talks to the robot on the local
     network and to Hugging Face with the user's own OAuth session; nothing is
     sent to the developer.
   - Encryption: answered in the Info.plist (`ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption`),
     ASC asks nothing per build.

4. **Developer ID Application certificate** (macOS) — Xcode → Settings →
   Accounts → Manage Certificates → “+” → Developer ID Application.

5. **macOS ships through both channels**, so the Mac App Store one needs its own
   signing assets besides the Developer ID certificate: Apple Distribution and
   Mac Installer Distribution. `-allowProvisioningUpdates` creates them through
   the Xcode account the same way it does for iOS. The app record already
   carries a macOS platform beside the iOS one — `mise run asc -- versions list
   --app 6799644194` shows both — so nothing has to be created in App Store
   Connect. What is not automatic is the App Group: step 2 registers it per App
   ID, and the macOS App ID is a separate one from the iOS App ID.

## Each release

1. Bump `MARKETING_VERSION` in `Apps/Project.swift` (bare semver, e.g. `0.2.0`)
   and land it on `main`. Build numbers are the commit count — nothing to bump.
2. Tag and push; the tag triggers the GitHub release with git-cliff notes:

   ```bash
   git tag 0.2.0 && git push origin 0.2.0
   ```

3. Produce and ship the artifacts:

   ```bash
   mise run release:ios     # archive → TestFlight
   mise run release:macos   # archive → both macOS channels (see below)
   gh release upload 0.2.0 Apps/DerivedData/Export/macOS/HeyReachy-0.2.0.zip
   ```

`release:macos` archives once and exports that archive twice, because
`-exportArchive` re-signs per method — the two artifacts are the same build:

| Channel        | Method            | Artifact                           | Ends up in              |
| -------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `developer-id` | notarize → staple | `Export/macOS/HeyReachy-<ver>.zip` | GitHub release, by hand |
| `appstore`     | upload            | `.pkg` (not kept)                  | TestFlight for macOS    |

Developer ID runs first on purpose: it is the artifact that always ships, and a
failed App Store upload should not also cost you the zip. Pick one channel with
`--channel appstore` or `--channel developer-id`.

Dry runs: `mise run release:ios -- --no-upload` exports an `.ipa` without
uploading; `mise run release:macos -- --no-notarize` stops the Developer ID
channel after the signed export, and `--no-upload` makes the App Store channel
leave a `.pkg` in `Export/macOS/AppStore` instead of uploading it. Each flag
belongs to one channel and is ignored by the other.

## Querying App Store Connect

`mise run asc` is the App Store Connect CLI with the same key already loaded —
`Scripts/asc.sh` maps the `REACHY_ASC_*` values onto the `ASC_*` names the tool
reads, so nothing is stored twice and no keychain profile exists to drift.
Everything after `--` goes to `asc`:

```bash
mise run asc -- apps list
mise run asc -- builds list --app 6799644194   # did the TestFlight upload land?
mise run asc -- testflight beta-groups list --app 6799644194
```

`asc` resolves a stored profile before the environment, so an `asc auth login`
run by hand silently outranks this wrapper — `mise run asc -- auth status`
prints which of the two is answering. The key is App Manager, not Admin, so the
same limit release-ios.sh documents applies: it can read and submit, and it
cannot manage provisioning profiles.

The CLI also ships 23 agent skills (`asc install-skills`, pinned to a reviewed
commit) covering TestFlight, metadata, submissions and signing.

## Xcode Cloud (optional, continuous TestFlight)

`Apps/ci_scripts/ci_post_clone.sh` makes a generated project buildable on
Xcode Cloud: it installs the pinned tools through the committed `bin/mise`
bootstrap, generates the workspace, and stamps `CI_BUILD_NUMBER` in as the
build number. Signing there is managed by Apple — no certificates leave the
account — and TestFlight distribution is a post-action checkbox. The setup
quirks (create the workflow from a local Xcode, start the build counter above
the last local upload, Git LFS is unsupported so never build the snapshot
scheme there) are commented at the top of the script.

`main` in `alexey1312/reachy-mini-swift` has no branch protection at all — the protection API answers
404 "Branch not protected". So `gh pr merge <n> --squash --auto` does **not** wait for anything: with no
required status checks there is nothing to block on, and the PR merges the moment the command runs, even
with jobs still `pending`. On PR #42 it landed while `App Build` and `Smoke` were mid-run.

**Why:** `--auto` queues on *required* checks. Zero required checks means the queue is already satisfied.
The flag reads as "merge when green" and behaves as "merge now".

**How to apply:** to actually wait for CI, poll `gh pr checks <n>` yourself and merge only once every job
reports `pass` — `--watch` blocks longer than a single tool timeout on this repo (App Build and the
preview build each run several minutes), so poll in rounds rather than watching once. Only reach for
`--auto` as fire-and-forget when merging ahead of CI is acceptable, as it was for a docs-only change.
See [[umbrella-branch-over-many-prs]] for when a PR is warranted at all here.

Влито и отправлено.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `--auto` не сработал так, как читается. У `main` нет branch protection вообще (API отдаёт 404 «Branch not protected»), а `--auto` ждёт только **required** checks. Нет обязательных — очередь считается пустой, и PR влился мгновенно, при живых `App Build` и `Smoke`. Записал в память, чтобы в следующий раз опрашивать `gh pr checks` руками.
- Для docs-only это без последствий: `Lint`, `Build & Test (macOS)` и `Preview Build` прошли до мержа, а два оставшихся джоба компилируют Swift, которого в диффе нет. Но если бы правка трогала код — я влил бы вслепую.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Что в итоге

`main` на `2c6df1b`, `docs/privacy.md` отдаёт HTTP 200 — проверил перед отправкой, потому что именно на 404 ревью и падает.

| Билд | Платформа | Состояние |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `10b9fbb3…` | iOS 0.1.1 (110) | `WAITING_FOR_REVIEW` |
| `1e2a3e38…` | macOS 0.1.1 (110) | `WAITING_FOR_REVIEW` |

Ссылка живая: **https://testflight.apple.com/join/CGjefT9a** — и уже в README. Присоединиться по ней можно прямо сейчас, скачать — после одобрения. Beta App Review обычно отвечает за 24–48 часов, iOS и macOS независимо друг от друга.

## Незакрытые хвосты

**CI на слитом коммите ещё идёт** — `App Build` и `Smoke` в run [31381506294](https://github.com/alexey1312/reachy-mini-swift/actions/runs/31381506294). Скажи, если хочешь, чтобы я досмотрел.

**Заметки ревьюеру обещают созвон** с показом живого робота — ты это не подтверждал явно, я предложил и оставил. Убирается одной командой `testflight review edit --notes`.

**Демо-видео.** В README всё ещё «on its way», и в заметках я на него не сослался — но если Apple откажет с формулировкой «не смогли оценить», видео станет самым коротким путём к апелляции.
